watch_policy.rule: one 1348-byte window at each MEM1-valued i32 pointer argument of the entry signature, per case
watch_policy.size_basis: derived from the plan's field_widths: the body's furthest load reaches +0x541

source.control_strategy: breakpoint the function entry, every out-of-unit call site AND every indirect branch in its in-unit closure, the instruction after each, and the entry LR; read CTR (bctrl) or LR (blrl) at the branch, before it executes, to record the RESOLVED TARGET; terminate the case at the return with a stack-pointer guard
source.emulator: bundled Dolphin 2606-97 (dolphin/Dolphin.exe), Null video, CPU only
source.game_state: 2v2 sav reloaded with a pl0900 roster in slots [0, 1, 2, 3] (roster depth 6) + B/X/A press-release edges
exclusions: dispatch_green is ORTHOGONAL to oracle_green and STRICTLY WEAKER than it: no memory write set is compared

the ROM's function-pointer TABLES are seeded from the live console (see seeded_dispatch_tables) -- bytes the port is GIVEN. What the port must derive on its own is WHICH ENTRY it selects, which is the behaviour under test
a dispatched callee's own behaviour is NOT verified: an in-window target runs the port's own code, an out-of-window target is a stub replaying the console's return registers
a bridged (out-of-window) return is supplied to the port as the console's r3 word only; a non-i32 return width crossing the bridge is NOT reproduced

argument registers are recorded RAW (r3-r10, f1-f8). The EABI slot each frame argument occupies is allocated at replay time from the CLASSES THE PORT ITSELF DECLARES, so a wrong class reads a wrong register and goes red

site binding is EXACT only for a function with exactly one indirect call; with two or more the comparison names the function, because Ghidra's structured C need not order sites as the machine code does
console stack addresses are excluded (the wasm module has its own linear stack)
the claim is bounded by this corpus -- N recorded cases, never all inputs
